claim.statement: Kimera-SWM's Walker seeds each cognitive walk with a maximally-distinctive concept from the source paragraph — specifically, a hapax-or-near-hapax (rarest concept in the corpus run). The Latinate appearance of position-0 concepts is a consequence of rare Shakespeare words being morphologically longer, not the primary mechanism.
claim.operationalization: Across 265 full-walk cycles from pg100.txt prose paragraphs: count cycles where position-0 concept has global frequency < 5 (rarity threshold). Null comparison: within-walk position shuffle (10,000 trials) of mean concept length. Cosine alternative tested: position-0 is highest-cosine to paragraph centroid only 20% of cycles, ruling out 'centroid-closest' rule.
claim.h0: Position-0 concept frequency distribution matches non-position-0 (no opener bias)
claim.h1: Position-0 systematically biased toward rare/distinctive concepts

preregistration.analysis_plan: Multi-hypothesis test: H_LEN, H_PROMPT, H_END, H_FREQ, H_NOV, H_COS_CENTROID against position-0 vs non-position-0 statistics.

detail.note: ruling-out test: position-0 is NOT centroid-closest

verdict.reasoning: Observed 90.6% of position-0 concepts have global frequency < 5; 68.3% are true hapaxes (freq=1); median position-0 freq=1 vs median position-rest freq=3. Within-walk shuffle null: position-0 mean concept length 8.51 vs null 5.81, z=22.5, p<1/10000. Cosine-to-centroid test: only 20% of position-0 are highest-cosine, ruling out centrality as mechanism.
